In [[mathematics]], two [[real number]]s  <math>p, q>1</math> are called '''conjugate indices''' (or '''Hölder conjugates''') if 

: <math>\frac{1}{p} + \frac{1}{q} = 1.</math> 

Formally, we also define  <math>q = \infty</math> as conjugate to <math>p=1</math> and [[List of Latin phrases: V#vice versa|vice versa]]. 

Conjugate indices are used in [[Hölder's inequality]], as well as [[Young's inequality for products]]; the latter can be used to prove the former. If <math>p, q>1</math> are conjugate indices, the spaces ''L''<sup>''p''</sup> and ''L''<sup>''q''</sup> are [[dual space|dual]] to each other (see [[Lp space|''L''<sup>''p''</sup> space]]).

==Properties==

The following are equivalent characterizations of Hölder conjugates:
* <math>\frac{1}{p} + \frac{1}{q} = 1,</math> 
* <math>pq = p + q,</math> 
* <math>\frac{p}{q} = p - 1,</math>
* <math>\frac{q}{p} = q - 1.</math>
